Synthetic fixtures for the Documents "Import from JSON" tests
(tests/documents-import-json.test.mjs, tests/documents-export-category.test.mjs).
Nothing here comes from a real database.

- valid-documents.json   four importable documents: Markdown with a bash code
                         fence, a mermaid block, a table, Unicode/emoji and
                         escapes (title+content), a locked Unicode-titled one,
                         a content-only one (no category -> General) and a
                         title-only one
- single-document.json   ONE document object, not an array (rejected with a
                         pointed "wrap it in [ ... ]" message)
- database-backup.json   the shape Export Database writes (rejected: points
                         the user to Import Database / the "documents" array)
- malformed.json         truncated JSON (SyntaxError)
- empty-array.json       [] (nothing to import)
- empty-file.json        zero bytes
- invalid-items.json     an array whose items are wrong in every way the
                         validator reports: missing title+content, null, a
                         string, a numeric title - plus one fine document that
                         must NOT be written when the file is rejected
- documents-with-images.json
                         the Export Category (JSON) shape WITH embedded
                         images: per-document `media` entries (filename,
                         mimeType, size, uploadedAt, tags, data = base64 data
                         URL, same encoding as the DB backup's media rows).
                         Two 1x1 PNGs generated by a few lines of Python
                         (red and blue dots): one image private to the first
                         document, one shared by two documents (with and
                         without a ?width= suffix), one reference whose image
                         was missing at export time, and a text-only document
